checklist.detail: Inconel 718 Nickel Superalloy: computed wall temp 1309 K EXCEEDS its 1250 K max service temp (Tc 3681 K, regenerative cooling). Marginal/unsuitable as designed. Basis: coupled throat wall balance: gas h_g ~10.9 kW/m2K incl. carbon-deposit credit, T_aw ~3623 K, coolant ~37 m/s (coolant-side wall ~974 K), 0.20 mm wall. Levers that lower it: faster coolant (Coolant velocity; SP-8087 caps liquids at ~61 m/s, at a jacket-dP cost), a thinner wall, a liner rated hotter or more conductive (e.g. GRCop-84), or more film cooling.

checklist.detail: Hottest wall station is in the convergent section (area ratio ~1.1, regen): wall ~1326 K, 0.94x that section's material limit (warns below 1.15x, like the throat row). Levers: more chamber film (or a convergent film ring for the throat region), faster coolant, a thinner or more conductive liner, or extend active cooling.

checklist.detail: OK - primary hoop stress ~122 MPa (~15.1 MPa net jacket-vs-gas differential, Huzel eq 4-27/4-28, tube_wall) vs a ~133 MPa allowable at the end of active cooling (area ratio ~18.0) (Inconel 718 Nickel Superalloy, SF 1.5, wall ~0.51 mm). The thermal-restraint stress (~622 MPa at the throat, dT = q*t/k across the wall) is a self-limiting secondary stress, not a burst load: with the hoop load it exceeds Inconel 718 Nickel Superalloy's ~200 MPa hot yield, so the hot face yields a little each firing - expected for a regen tube wall (the real F-1/J-2/RL10 do the same in this model). Its life limit is the 'Throat thermal-fatigue cycle life' row.
